final_answer: The mRNA vaccine process begins with injection into the muscle. The vaccine contains mRNA enclosed in lipid nanoparticles, which protect the mRNA from degradation. Once injected, the lipid nanoparticles fuse with cell membranes, releasing the mRNA into the cytoplasm. The cell's ribosomes then read the mRNA sequence, producing viral proteins (e.g., the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2). These proteins are displayed on the cell surface, alerting the immune system. Dendritic cells capture the viral proteins, process them, and present fragments to T-cells and B-cells. B-cells generate antibodies specific to the viral protein, while T-cells activate to destroy infected cells. Memory B-cells and T-cells remain in the body, enabling a rapid response upon future exposure to the virus. The mRNA is degraded after protein synthesis, ensuring no integration into the host genome.
